subject: URGENT: BlueWave - sustained 5xx and latency spike in us-east-3
messages:
From: ops@bluewave.ai
To: mina.haddad@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@bluewave.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Nov 2028 15:07:00 +0000
Subject: URGENT: BlueWave - sustained 5xx and latency spike in us-east-3

Mina,

We are seeing a sustained surge of 5xx errors and tail latency from ~14:50 UTC in us-east-3 (AZ3). Error rate is currently ~48% on our production tokenization endpoint and p95 latency has gone from ~80ms up to ~1.5s. This started after a normal deploy on our side (no changes on Redwood) but the traffic pattern shouldn’t cause this. Our SLOs are impacted and customers are complaining.

Can you confirm whether there's any known AZ3 degradation on Redwood? We need immediate mitigation: can you either (a) fail traffic to us-east-1/us-west-2, or (b) whitelist us for burst capacity to reduce queueing? We will need an incident summary and proposed timeline for mitigation.

We’ve attached a small snapshot of our error logs and a screenshot of the dashboard.

Attachments: ops_snapshot.txt, metrics_dashboard_screenshot.png

Thanks,
Aaron Singh
ops@bluewave.ai
BlueWave Analytics
From: mina.haddad@redwood.com
To: ops@bluewave.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Nov 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: BlueWave - sustained 5xx and latency spike in us-east-3

Aaron — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We’re escalating immediately. I’ve looped in our on-call infra lead (Hannah) and ops (Vanessa) and the account lead (Rishi).

Immediate plan:
- Hannah will validate whether AZ3 is experiencing platform-level issues and check our regional load balancer health and NIC metrics.
- If this is an AZ3 capacity/saturation issue we will initiate a customer-directed cross-region failover for BW production to us-east-1 within the next 20–30 minutes.
- I’ll follow up with proposed credit/compensation language once we have a mitigation timeline.

Please keep the log exports coming. I’ll update in 15 minutes.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198
From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
To: mina.haddad@redwood.com, ops@bluewave.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, infra-oncall@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Nov 2028 15:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: BlueWave - sustained 5xx and latency spike in us-east-3

Mina / Aaron — quick technical update from infra: we see a clear spike in packet drops and RX errors on a subset of AZ3 hosts starting ~14:48 UTC correlated with a set of customer batch inference jobs that unexpectedly saturated NIC bandwidth for that AZ. Tail latencies and 502/503s are consistent with queue head-of-line blocking in the serving fleet.

What we’re doing now:
- Kicked a targeted drain of BW request routes off the impacted AZ3 subpool and started failover to us-east-1 (traffic-steer rule: region fallback).
- Applied temporary per-customer rate smoothing for BW to prevent amplifying retries.
- Spun up two temporary instances in us-east-1 with a compatible model variant (quantized) to accept burst traffic — expected warm-up ~7–10 minutes.

Attachments: runbook_failover.pdf, ops_snapshot.txt (annotated)

Impact estimate: we expect error rate to fall below 3% for BW after traffic completes rehome and the new instances warm (target 15–25 minutes). If packet drops persist at the infra level in AZ3 we’ll keep traffic redirected until the cloud provider confirms NIC stability.

I’ll post another update at +30m or earlier if anything changes.

— Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
From: mina.haddad@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, ops@bluewave.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Nov 2028 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: BlueWave - sustained 5xx and latency spike in us-east-3

Team / Aaron — summary and action ask for exec:

Summary: AZ3 experienced NIC-level saturation starting ~14:48 UTC which caused queueing and a high 5xx rate for BlueWave. Engineering (Hannah) has initiated a targeted drain and is routing BW to warmed instances in us-east-1. Early telemetry: p95 latency trending down, error rate moving from ~48% to ~12% during redirection.

Ask (exec / sales approval):
1) Approve a proactive full-region rehome (us-east-3 -> us-east-1) if error rate does not drop below 5% within 30 minutes. This may change billing footprint for the short term (cross-region egress) and we should authorize emergency credits if customer requests.
2) Approve a one-time service credit up to 7% of last month’s invoice (or equivalent pro-rated credit) as a gesture of goodwill should BlueWave request formal compensation — I recommend offering 3–5% now and escalating to 7% if customer demand escalates.

I’ve added the incident runbook and the annotated ops snapshot to the thread. Hannah — please confirm when traffic is fully redirected and whether we need an extended time window.

Aaron — apologies for the disruption. We’re treating this as P0. Rishi and I will handle commercial comms; Vanessa will support any procurement/contract questions.

— Mina

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: ceo@bluewave.ai, ops@bluewave.ai
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Nov 2028 18:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: BlueWave - sustained 5xx and latency spike in us-east-3 — Next steps and credit

Hi Aaron / Alex — I’m Rishi (acct lead for BlueWave). Thank you for the quick escalation; I’m sorry for the disruption. Per Mina and Hannah: traffic was routed off the impacted AZ and the new instances in us-east-1 have accepted the load. Current telemetry: error rate ~1.9%, p95 latency ~95ms.

Commercial note: we want to make this right. We will offer an immediate credit of 4% of November’s invoice applied to your December billing. If you’d like a formal RFP for longer-term dedicated capacity or reserved capacity to reduce future risk, I can set up a time this week to review options and costs.

Next steps we will share in the incident report (ETA 24 hours): timeline of events, root-cause analysis, and mitigation steps including a post-mortem on how to prevent NIC saturation (rate-limits on batch jobs, improved per-tenant isolation).

If you want traffic moved back to us-east-3 after the cloud provider confirms NIC health, we’ll coordinate a controlled rehome window.

Thanks again; I’ll follow up with a short exec summary.

— Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
(end of thread)
